title: The Semester of Lake Minnow
premise: Mirabel Nakamura, seventeen and de facto parent to two younger siblings while their mother works hospital night shifts, has perfected the art of 'fine.' But when Lake Minnow High's legendary drowned ghost begins leaving notes in ink that vanishes by morning — notes that know Mirabel's name, her secrets, her sister's asthma — Mirabel is dragged into a decades-old cover-up involving the school's beloved founding principal. As the ghost's demands escalate toward exposing a truth that would destroy the reputation of Mirabel's best friend's family, Mirabel must choose between protecting everyone and telling the truth. In the end, Mirabel confesses everything — including how badly they've been drowning themselves — losing the friendship but gaining an honest found family of misfits who help lay the ghost to rest before prom.
about_author: Petra Underhill grew up in a lakeside mill town where every local legend had at least three contradictory versions. She writes stories about kids holding families together with tape and stubbornness.

chapters.title: Fine Is a Full-Time Job
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A chaotic morning — burnt toast, little brother Theo's lost permission slip, sister Juno's forgotten inhaler — establishes Mirabel's exhausting competence and cheerful denial. Emotional beat: loving warmth laced with quiet dread as Mirabel insists, again, that everything is fine.

chapters.title: The Legend According to Everyone
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At school, friends debate the Lake Minnow ghost: a student who drowned in 1968, said to haunt the old east wing. Best friend Dana dismisses it; new kid Wren collects ghost lore like currency. Emotional beat: playful camaraderie that subtly shows Mirabel standing slightly outside the group.

chapters.title: Ink That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Detention duty in the east wing, Mirabel finds a note on their desk: 'You count the stairs so no one falls behind you. I see you, Mirabel Nakamura.' The ink shimmers green, then fades. Emotional beat: uncanny vertigo — being seen for the first time feels terrifyingly good.

chapters.title: Rules for Hauntings
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, who has moved eleven times and catalogued ghosts in six towns, recognizes impossible ink when they see it. They approach Mirabel with a binder of evidence. Emotional beat: tentative connection between two kids who've both learned to observe rather than belong.

chapters.title: What Juno Saw
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Twelve-year-old Juno admits she saw a figure by the pool last week — and that it mouthed her name. Mirabel shuts it down hard, terrified. Emotional beat: sibling friction revealing Mirabel's protective instinct curdling into control.

chapters.title: The Principal's Portrait
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Wren's alternating POV. Research reveals founding principal Edmund Voss, hero of every hallway plaque, was principal during the 1968 drowning. His portrait's eyes seem to follow them. Emotional beat: first thrill of shared investigation, and the first hint that the town's cherished story doesn't hold.

chapters.title: Second Note, Sharper Teeth
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A new note appears inside Mirabel's locker: 'Ask Voss what he kept in the boathouse.' That night Mom misses dinner again; Mirabel lies to Theo about why. Emotional beat: the haunting and home life begin mirroring each other — secrets stacked on secrets.

chapters.title: Dana's Family Name
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The boathouse records implicate the Hollis family — Dana's family — in covering up the drowning. Dana's grandfather was Voss's protégé. Emotional beat: cold dread as the mystery stops being academic and starts aiming at the person Mirabel loves most.

chapters.title: The Pool at Midnight
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Mirabel break into the natatorium and meet the ghost properly: a girl, Ruth Okafor, soaked and furious, who shows them a memory — she didn't slip; she was pushed during a hazing ritual Voss tolerated. Emotional beat: awe giving way to horror; the legend was a lie told on purpose.

chapters.title: Everyone Knows Except Us
chapters.summary: Multiple short POVs (Theo, Juno, teacher Ms. Adeyemi). The town's complicity surfaces: yearbooks altered, a scholarship named for Voss, teachers who 'don't discuss it.' Emotional beat: creeping realization that corruption isn't one villain but a whole ecosystem of convenience.

chapters.title: Promises Made in Green Ink
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Ruth offers a bargain: bring her story into daylight by prom night, or she starts leaving notes for everyone — including Juno. Mirabel agrees, hiding the deadline from Wren. Emotional beat: power corrupting gently; Mirabel becomes the thing they hate, managing truth like a parent manages bad news.

chapters.title: The Friend Who Can't Hear It
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Dana senses Mirabel pulling away, plans prom, talks about her grandfather's legacy award. Mirabel almost tells her twice and swallows it. Emotional beat: aching dramatic irony; the reader feels the friendship cracking under weight Dana can't see.

chapters.title: Little Lies, Big House
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Juno discovers Mirabel's hidden notes and research, feels betrayed by being protected from the truth. She confronts Mirabel: 'You treat us like we're made of glass.' Emotional beat: the found-family theme turns inward — Mirabel must learn family means honesty, not shelter.

chapters.title: Voss's Box
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Wren's POV. In the flooded sub-basement archive they find Voss's locked box: Ruth's real report, suppressed; letters showing the Hollis patriarch helped bury it in exchange for funding. Emotional beat: triumph immediately soured by cost — this proof will burn Dana's world down.

chapters.title: The Offer You Shouldn't Take
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Dana's father privately offers Mirabel a college fund and a quiet apartment 'for the kids' if certain documents stay buried. For one dizzy hour, Mirabel considers it — rent, groceries, rest. Emotional beat: temptation rendered tenderly; corruption rarely looks like evil, it looks like relief.

chapters.title: What Mirabel Almost Did
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds the signed nondisclosure draft in Mirabel's backpack and calls it out, not with anger but heartbreak: 'You're becoming the people who drowned her.' Emotional beat: lowest point; Mirabel alone, friendless-feeling, staring at the lake.

chapters.title: Ruth's Side of the Water
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV (a luminous interlude). Ruth remembers being seventeen, ambitious, silenced — and admits her rage has been curdling into the same coercion she suffered. She sees herself in Mirabel's bargain. Emotional beat: the ghost confronts her own corruption; grief without accountability, she realizes, just drowns others.

chapters.title: Telling the Truth Out Loud
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel gathers Wren, Juno, Theo, and finally Dana, and tells everything — the notes, the box, the offer, and their own near-betrayal. Dana walks out. Emotional beat: devastating honesty; the blurb's promise fulfilled — truth costs the friendship, and Mirabel pays it anyway.

chapters.title: Prom Night, East Wing
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. On prom night, the group (minus Dana) stages a public reading of Ruth's report in the gym, projected beside Voss's portrait, while Ruth manifests visibly for one minute. The school freezes; Ms. Adeyemi backs them with the archived originals. Emotional beat: climax — courage as collective act, not solo heroics.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Green Ink
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Fallout: the district investigates, the Voss name comes off plaques, Dana's family fractures — and Dana, weeks later, leaves one final note in fading green ink: 'I'm not ready to forgive you. But I believe you.' Emotional beat: grief and grace coexisting; not all wounds close neatly.

chapters.title: Laying Her Down
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The group holds a small ceremony at the lake — Juno reads a poem, Theo drops paper boats, Wren archives everything publicly online. Ruth's presence lifts like fog at sunrise. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into memory; the ghost finally gets witnesses instead of rumors.

chapters.title: The Semester After
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Summer: Mom switches to day shifts, Mirabel joins a youth advocacy group Wren started, and Dana shows up at the door with two coffees and no promises. Mirabel still counts the stairs — but now, so does everyone. Emotional beat: resolution — 'fine' replaced by something better: true, shared, and still under construction.
